title: The Crooked Sigil
premise: Felix Galloway, the last apprentice of the Ledgerkeepers—a guild that records and trades in impossible things—discovers that a child who arrives at their door speaks the First Tongue, the language in which souls are written. The child's soul was sold to the court beneath the mountain by the usurper Veyra, who is buying First Tongue speakers to fuel her conquest of the free cities. With the guild's fractious remnants—an exiled forger, a disgraced knight, and the guildmaster who lied about why the ledgers matter—Felix must forge an entry into the underworld court, steal the soul back from its vault of names, and rewrite it before Veyra's armies arrive. They succeed at terrible cost: the guildmaster gives his own name in exchange, the guild dissolves into something new, and Felix learns that belonging is not inherited but chosen.
about_author: J. M. Joubert is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing obscure trade guilds before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about paperwork, loyalty, and the quiet violence of institutions.

chapters.title: The Weight of Unwritten Things
chapters.summary: POV Felix. The Ledgerkeepers' hall is nearly empty; Felix catalogs relics no one buys while guildmaster Corvane drinks. A mud-soaked child appears at the door speaking a language that makes the ledger ink crawl. Emotional beat: loneliness cracked open by wonder—the first time Felix feels needed.

chapters.title: A Grammar of Souls
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Corvane recognizes the First Tongue and lies badly about it. The child, Wren, draws sigils that match entries in the sealed Black Ledger. Felix secretly copies them, discovering Wren's soul-page is missing—sold. Emotional beat: dread as duty curdles into complicity.

chapters.title: The Forger's Debt
chapters.summary: POV Sable, the exiled forger living above a dye-house. Corvane calls in her old debt: she once forged a death record for him. She agrees to help only after seeing Wren's sigils and recognizing the hand of the court beneath the mountain. Emotional beat: resentment giving way to reluctant protectiveness.

chapters.title: What the Knight Buried
chapters.summary: POV Dame Ivetta, a knight who refused Veyra's purge and lost everything. She interrogates Felix, suspecting the guild of treason, then finds proof Veyra is harvesting First Tongue speakers. She defects with her testimony instead of arresting them. Emotional beat: shame transformed into purpose.

chapters.title: The Road Under the World
chapters.summary: POV Felix. The four flee ahead of Veyra's vanguard through the sunken roads, guided by Wren's instinctive fluency. An ambush by Veyra's name-takers costs them their supplies and nearly Wren. Emotional beat: found family forged under fire—bickering becomes trust.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: POV Sable. They reach the underworld court, where souls are traded as currency and every visitor must surrender one true memory at the gate. Sable pays with the memory of her sister. Emotional beat: awe and horror—the price of entry made flesh.

chapters.title: The Vault of Names
chapters.summary: POV Ivetta. Using her knight's standing as cover, Ivetta infiltrates the vault while Felix and Sable forge a false ledger entry to swap for Wren's soul. The forgery works—until Corvane's old lie surfaces and the court brands them thieves. Emotional beat: triumph snatched away mid-breath.

chapters.title: Every Debt Comes Due
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Captured, Felix bargains with the court's magistrate using the Black Ledger itself, revealing Corvane sold Wren's soul years ago to save the guild. Corvane confesses and offers his own name in Wren's place. Emotional beat: betrayal and forgiveness colliding—justice outside any law.

chapters.title: The Rewriting
chapters.summary: POV Wren. In the vault, Wren speaks their own true name aloud for the first time, and Felix writes it back into being as Veyra's armies breach the mountain above. The court shakes; the vault of names begins to empty. Emotional beat: terror and fierce joy—selfhood reclaimed.

chapters.title: A New Entry in the Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Felix. They surface to find Veyra's advance broken by freed name-takers turning on her. Corvane is gone, remembered by no one but them. The survivors reopen the guildhall—not as traders in souls, but as keepers who return them. Emotional beat: grief braided with belonging; an ending that is also a beginning.
